text:
alex: Quick audit — noticed kernel selection flips between fastpath_v2 and slowpath_compat on A100S at seq_len=128. Might be tied to our SM/feature detection order. Anyone seen this in recent canaries?

lina: I saw a similar blip last night but assumed it was KV cache thrash. Do we have the perf traces? :eyes:

perf-bot: autotune-log 1748889000:
```
hw_signature: SM86
driver: 525.60
tensor_cores: true
bf16: true
fp8: false
selected_kernel: slowpath_compat
reason: kernel_perf_estimate (kv_hotness > 0.7)
```

matt: KV cache hotness >0.7 explains the fallback. But the latency delta between the two kernels at p50 is tiny; p99 regressed a lot. Looks like batching heuristic + KV eviction pattern kills fastpath.

alex: here's a quick microbench from staging (single-GPU, 16 batch):
```
seq_len | kernel            | p50(ms) | p99(ms) | throughput(tokens/s)
64      | fastpath_v2       | 6.2     | 12.1    | 420k
128     | slowpath_compat   | 9.8     | 35.4    | 380k
128     | fastpath_v2 (no-kv) | 9.0  | 28.1    | 395k
```
Note: forcing KV cache disabled improves p99.

lina: That suggests KV interactions with kernel memory layout. Two quick proposals: 1) change detection order to prioritize compute capability/TC presence before KV heuristics; 2) expose a per-model kv_hotness override in the autotune profile.

matt: +1 on the profile override. For detection order, can we do this defensively? i.e., keep current heuristic but record a conflict metric so we can roll back if regressions spike.

alex: Proposed change (pseudo):
```
if (sm_major >= 8 && tensor_cores) {
  enable_fastpath_candidate();
}
estimate = kernel_cost_estimator(...);
if (kv_hotness > threshold && estimate.fastpath_penalty > X) {
  pick(slowpath_compat);
} else {
  pick(fastpath_candidate);
}
```
I'll push a small patch to reorder the checks and add a conflict metric.

perf-bot: autotune-sim after patch:
"autotune_run_id": "run-1748889321-1",
"result": "fastpath_v3 chosen for seq<=128 on SM86",
"p99_improvement": "-7%",
"throughput_change": "+1.2% (median)",
"note": "under high kv churn throughput drops ~3%"

lina: FP8/driver probing note: newer driver reports fp8_supported=true for some microcode combos even if kernels don't actually benefit. We should add a verification microbench when fp8 flag is set before selecting fp8-optimized kernels.

matt: Agreed. Also add a metric 'kernel_conflict_rate' and 'kv_fallback_count' to perf logs. If conflict_rate > 0.5% for 10m, auto-fallback to safe path.

alex: I'll open the PR with the reordered checks, the conflict metric, and a canary plan. Canaries: staging 10% traffic to dedicated pool, monitor p99, conflict_rate, kv_fallback_count for 1h. Tagging @oncall to watch. :thumbsup:

oncall: okay — i'll watch the canary window and have rollback playbook ready. If p99 regresses >10% or kv_fallback_count spikes, i'll roll back.

matt: I'll also add a small autotune job to the weekly pipeline to re-evaluate kernel picks with synthetic kv churn. That should catch bitrot.

alex: SGTM. Thanks all — rolling PR in ~30m.
